name: Ramirez Clinical NLP Lab
researchArea: Clinical and multilingual NLP, LLM fine-tuning
notes: Deadline crunch lab (demo A). Gautschi bank down to ~3k H100-hours.
contextDump: We're a 7-person NLP group (CS). Funding: NSF CAREER (ends Aug 2028) bought us 2 H100 GPU-years on Gautschi (17,520 GPU-hours, resets July 1) and our department share is 4x A100-80GB on Gilbreth (account 'ramirez'). The Gautschi bank is nearly gone (~3,100 hours left) and there is no supplement until July, so please push anything that fits on 80GB A100s to Gilbreth first. IMMEDIATE: ICLR 2027 rebuttal experiments are due Friday Nov 20, 5 pm ET (LoRA fine-tunes of Llama-3-8B on ~40 GB of de-identified clinical notes). Next: ICML 2027 full paper Jan 28. Data: notes are de-identified but still under a hospital DUA - they must stay on Purdue storage (no AWS). Rules: final/thesis runs never on preemptible or standby; sweeps can use standby. Any single run over 500 GPU-hours needs my OK. We use bf16 + FlashAttention-2, so A100/H100 only; please don't put us on A30s.

name: Okafor Visual Computing Lab
notes: Runs mostly on NSF ACCESS credits (Anvil gpu/ai).
contextDump: ECE vision lab, 6 people. Most of our compute is an NSF ACCESS Discover award (CIS250417, 1.5M credits exchanged for Anvil CPU/GPU/AI, ends Mar 31 2027) - we've burned ~82% already, mostly on H100s on Anvil ai. A small startup share on Gilbreth (2x A100-40GB). Deadlines: CVPR 2027 supplementary + code release Nov 24, ICCV 2027 in early March. Our open-vocabulary 3D segmentation model trains on 4-8 GPUs for ~2 days; Anvil caps us at 12 GPUs per user and 32 per allocation, and 48 h walltime, so we chain jobs with checkpoints. Please warn me before we drop under 150k credits so I can file a supplement. Students tend to leave Jupyter sessions holding GPUs overnight - kill those.

name: Lindqvist Computational Chemistry Group
notes: Long CPU MD + GPU free-energy runs; demo C (preemption-safe 6-day run).
contextDump: Comp chem group, 8 members. We own 256 cores (2 half-node shares) on Negishi and 1 H100 GPU-year on Gautschi, plus an ACCESS Explore award on Anvil (CHE250114) for GROMACS/CP2K throughput. Typical jobs: multi-day MD (GROMACS, OpenMM) and DFT screening (CP2K, VASP) - CPU heavy, 2-14 days, MPI across 2-8 nodes. Our big one: 6-day alchemical free-energy MD of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitors for the JCTC revision (due Dec 18). Gautschi ai normal QOS dropped to 4 days on Nov 2, so long GPU runs must go preemptible with checkpoints every 30 min (OpenMM writes them; we requeue with --signal=B:USR1@600). Exploratory sweeps should always use standby. We don't care about speed as much as SU efficiency - cheapest plan unless a deadline is close.

name: Patel Structural Genomics Lab
researchArea: Pathogen protein structure prediction, single-cell ML
notes: Export-controlled data: Gilbreth only (no Anvil/ACCESS, no AWS).
contextDump: Structural genomics, 5 people, funded by a DTRA award plus NIH R01. IMPORTANT: the pathogen sequence set for Project HELIX is export-controlled (EAR) under our technology control plan. It may only be processed on Purdue-owned Gilbreth nodes under account 'patel' - never on Anvil/ACCESS, never on AWS or any cloud, and only by US-person lab members listed on the TCP. Our Gilbreth purchase is 4x A100-80GB + 2x A30. Workloads: AlphaFold-Multimer / ColabFold inference (1-2 GPUs, 2-10 h, GPU memory heavy for big complexes) and a single-cell foundation-model fine-tune (non-controlled data, can go anywhere). Deliverable: structure atlas to DTRA on Dec 1. RECOMB 2027 mid-February.

name: Haddad Robot Learning Lab
notes: Many short sim jobs; historically low GPU util (CPU-bound simulators).
contextDump: Robot learning lab (ME + ECE), 7 people, lots of undergrads. Compute: 1 H100 GPU-year on Gautschi (we mostly run preemptible at 0.25x so it stretches) plus 2x A30 on Gilbreth; L40S smallgpu for Isaac Lab rendering. Our PPO runs are simulator-bound: GPU util is often 20-40%, which RCAC has flagged before - recommend cheaper GPUs when util is low. Checkpoint every 20 min on preemptible. Quiet hours: weekdays 9am-5pm our 2 A30s are reserved for students debugging on the real robot, so batch training should go elsewhere then. Deadlines: thesis committee demo Dec 10, RSS 2027 end of January. Budget is tight; nobody should launch >8 GPUs without asking me.

name: Nguyen Regional Climate Modeling Group
contextDump: Regional climate group in EAPS, 12 people. Our workhorse is WRF (MPI, 4-56 nodes, 6-12 h per ensemble member) on Anvil under an ACCESS Accelerate award (EES250031, 3M credits, ~64% used, ends Mar 31 2027). We ran our post-processing on Bell for six years; Bell was retired Oct 31 and we are moving those scripts to Gautschi cpu (we bought 96 cores = 2 x 48-core units). Anvil scratch purges after 30 days with no warning - remind people to copy WRF output to Depot. Deadline: AGU Fall Meeting posters Dec 7 (CONUS 4-km ensemble must finish by Dec 2). Small ML emulator project on Anvil A100s. Wide queue only allows 12 h, so long members must checkpoint/restart.

name: Kowalski Digital Agriculture Lab
notes: Tiny budget; AWS research credits nearly exhausted (demo of budget burn).
contextDump: Small digital-ag lab (4 people). We don't own much: 1x A10 on Gilbreth from the department and $25,000 of AWS Cloud Credits for Research (expires Jan 14 2027) that we use for p4d bursts when Gilbreth is busy - about $1,200 left. Spot instances are fine for training (we checkpoint every epoch); on-demand only for the USDA demo. Drone imagery is not sensitive. USDA NIFA milestone report Nov 27 needs the canopy segmentation model retrained on the 2026 season (~1.2 TB of orthomosaics). Please stop anything that would overspend the credits - when they hit 95%, hold new AWS jobs and tell me.

name: Adeyemi Quantum Materials ML Lab
researchArea: Graph neural network foundation models for materials
notes: Biggest Gautschi H100 user; over fair share; demo B (idle GPUs + burn) and D (policy change).
contextDump: Quantum materials ML, 6 people. We bought the 5 GPU-year package on Gautschi ai (43,800 H100-hours this fiscal year, normal QOS cap max(2, 2x5) = 10 GPUs concurrently) and we are at ~88% used in November - burn is way ahead of plan. Main run: pretraining a 1.3B-parameter equivariant GNN on Materials Project + OMat24 (26B tokens-equivalent) on 8x H100 for the ICML 2027 deadline (Jan 28). Our 6-day jobs were legal before Nov 2; now normal QOS is 4 days, so they must be split or go preemptible. Dataloader is a known bottleneck (LMDB on scratch) - if GPUs sit idle, scale the job down rather than letting it burn. Notify me when projected burn would exhaust the bank before the deadline.
